title: Universal property of a power series ring mapping into a complete ring
statement: Let $\Lambda$ and $T$ be commutative rings, $\mathfrak a\subseteq T$ an ideal such that $T$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\alpha:\Lambda\to T$ a ring homomorphism, $n\ge0$, and $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathfrak a$. Write $t^E=t_1^{e_1}\cdots t_n^{e_n}$ and $|E|=e_1+\cdots+e_n$ for $E\in\mathbf N^n$. Then there is a ring homomorphism $\Phi:\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ from the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that $\Phi(\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$ (constant series) and $\Phi(x_i)=t_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$; for $F=\sum_Ea_Ex^E$, $\Phi(F)$ is the unique element of $T$ with $\Phi(F)\equiv\sum_{|E|<m}\alpha(a_E)t^E\pmod{\mathfrak a^m}$ for every $m\ge1$. Moreover $\Phi$ is the only ring homomorphism $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\to T$ which agrees with $\alpha$ on $\Lambda$ and sends $x_i$ to $t_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: used without statement as 'the universal property of power series rings' in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9719), in the proof of Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, line 9812: the map phi' : Lambda[[x]] -> S[[y]], x_i -> phi(x_i) + y_i) and in Algebra, proof of Theorem Tag 032A (algebra.tex line 45014: Lambda[[x_1..x_n]] -> R, x_i -> y_i); agent-formulated

proof.text: Construct for each m the ring homomorphism q_m by composing Mathlib MvPowerSeries.truncTotalAlgHom with Ideal.quotientMap of MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom α t. The variables ideal maps into a because t_i is in a, and Ideal.le_comap_pow sends its mth power into a^m. Mathlib truncTotal_sub_truncTotal_mem_pow_idealOfVars proves compatibility. IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom constructs Φ with these projections; no witness is chosen from an unproved theorem.

Use IsHausdorff.funext' to compare elements by all projections. Constant truncations equal the constant for m>0. Variable truncations equal X_i for m>1 and zero otherwise; t_i belongs to a and therefore to a^m for m≤1. The zero projection is trivial. This gives the prescribed values and the equivalence between all positive truncation congruences and y=Φ(F).

For any competing ring homomorphism Ψ, polynomial induction gives Ψ(p)=eval₂ α t p. Apply power_series_mem_combined_ideal_pow_iff with base ideal zero: the tail F-truncTotal m F has vanishing coefficients below m, so lies in (X)^m. Since Ψ(X_i)=t_i is in a, Ideal.le_comap_pow sends this tail into a^m. Thus Ψ and Φ have equal projections for every m; separatedness gives Ψ=Φ. No continuity hypothesis is used.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against its uses: lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-flat-presentation step 3 uses existence with the values on Lambda and x_i, step 4 the uniqueness among all ring maps; lem-weil-pbc-cohen-structure-power-series-surjection step 5 uses existence and the values, step 6 only that Phi is a ring map with Phi(x^E)=y^E). No sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration states it (grep of WeilConjectures for the id, MvPowerSeries with eval/IsAdicComplete: none). No Stacks lemma states it (used without statement in 07NL, 07NN, 032A), so the proof is written by an agent from the two definition nodes, in six elementary steps: (1) partial sums P_m(F) and P_m' - P_m in a^m; (2) completeness (bijectivity of T -> lim T/a^m) gives Phi(F) with Phi(F) = P_m(F) mod a^m, unique, and the intersection of the a^m is 0; (3) Phi additive, unital, multiplicative via P_m(F)P_m(G) = P_m(FG) mod a^m; (4) Phi(lambda)=alpha(lambda), Phi(x_i)=t_i; (5) a series with no terms of degree < m is a finite sum of x^E g_E with |E|=m (explicit g_E); (6) any ring map Phi' with these values satisfies Phi'(F) = P_m(F) mod a^m, hence Phi'=Phi, no continuity assumed. Source line numbers corrected: 07NN map phi' is at more-algebra.tex line 9812 (not 9769), 032A's map at algebra.tex line 45014 (not 44929).
